concepts.why: The presence of a unilocular radiolucent lesion with an irregular shape and buccolingual expansion is consistent with an odontogenic keratocyst.
The location of the radiolucent lesion at the apex of a previously endodontically treated tooth is consistent with a radicular cyst.
The presence of a unilocular radiolucent lesion with buccolingual expansion is consistent with a unicystic ameloblastoma.
The presence of tender teeth and a radiolucent lesion at the apex of a tooth is consistent with a periapical granuloma.

rationales.F02: Tender percussion is more typical of radicular cysts and periapical granulomas.
rationales.F06: A unilocular radiolucent lesion is common in all three main differential diagnoses.
rationales.F07: The irregular shape is atypical for routine periapical cysts or granulomas, making odontogenic keratocyst and unicystic ameloblastoma more likely.
rationales.F08: Buccolingual expansion with almost complete obliteration of the lingual cortex is more characteristic of aggressive lesions like unicystic ameloblastoma and odontogenic keratocyst.
rationales.F10: The preliminary differential diagnosis already includes odontogenic keratocyst, radicular cyst, and unicystic ameloblastoma, making them more likely by definition.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of a unilocular radiolucent lesion with buccolingual expansion and almost complete obliteration of the lingual cortex, along with its irregular shape, supports the diagnosis of odontogenic keratocyst over other options.
